evidence: hypothesis integration test 250% margin with significant zero-effect test

mapping.implementation: Explicit repeat count and seed via library, attributes and direct Cargo; nonzero Monte Carlo probability correction; degenerate null draws counted rather than removed

differences: Independent processes are sampling units; within-process batches cannot inflate significance. Criterion uses its timing samples.
Airbug uses process medians as inputs to Welch and retains its existing median-interval practical-change decisions. p-values and practical margins answer distinct questions.
Distinct constant groups with zero variance produce an unavailable Welch test. Equal constant groups yield p=1.
Paired A/B analysis is an Airbug extension; no paired comparison API was found in the audited Criterion/Divan surface, so its interval method does not block this parity item.

tracked_elsewhere.plots: Welch distribution rendering and export are implemented; final visual acceptance remains in plots.json.
tracked_elsewhere.artifacts: Retained null draws export is implemented; final report artifact acceptance remains in artifacts.json.

source_semantic_audit.capabilities: Welch statistic, pooled null resampling, configurable significance, practical effect threshold, relative estimates and reported uncertainty are available natively.
native_differences: Criterion discards nonfinite null draws, then computes twice the smaller empirical tail using a strict x < t count. Airbug compares absolute statistics, retains degenerate outcomes, and applies (extreme + 1)/(resamples + 1). Finite-sample p-values are not identical.

Criterion gates its improved/regressed/no-change wording by p-value and then the relative mean interval versus its noise threshold. Airbug reports zero-effect hypothesis and practical median-interval decision separately.
Airbug family-adjusts significance for multiple comparisons and reports the effective alpha. Independent process medians are its inferential units; one-process batch changes remain exploratory.
Seeded native resampling makes repeated analyses reproducible; no upstream random-stream compatibility is claimed.
source_semantic_audit.validation: Three all-feature hypothesis integration tests passed on macOS; numerical oracle tests are covered by the latest 521-test MSRV gate.

matched_formulas: Median and percentile bounds using linear interpolation over sorted observations
Sample standard deviation with n-1 denominator
Bootstrap standard error from the sample standard deviation of retained estimates
native_differences: Airbug normalizes by maximum absolute value internally to limit overflow, then restores original units. Floating-point rounding and random streams need not match upstream.
A single observation has descriptive location values but no sample standard deviation or bootstrap interval; a single resample has unavailable standard error.
Airbug labels the statistical population: normalized batches for one process, equally weighted process medians for multiple processes.
descriptive_estimates_audit.validation: All 12 bootstrap::tests tests passed on macOS, covering known point values, retained resample oracles, standard errors, constant/single/large values, confidence settings, population labels and parallel determinism.

matched_capabilities: Percentile slope interval and bootstrap standard error
Goodness of fit at point slope and confidence-bound endpoints
native_differences: Airbug scales coordinates to limit overflow and reports unavailable goodness for constant totals; negative R-squared is preserved.

Pinned Criterion Slope::r_squared assigns ss_tot = ss_res + (y - y_bar)^2 inside its loop. Airbug uses centered total variation sum((y - mean)^2), independently checked as 1 - SSE/SST. Numeric identity to that upstream implementation is not claimed.
Airbug fits each process separately; no pooling of within-process paired batches into independent process repetitions.
regression_semantic_audit.validation: Eight all-feature regression tests passed: exact/noisy oracles, paired resamples, endpoint goodness, scale invariance, negative/undefined R-squared, saved pairs and deterministic parallel analysis.

matched_contracts: Mild fences at 1.5 IQR and severe fences at 3 IQR
Strict comparisons: a point exactly on a fence belongs to the less severe class
Original observation order and all five class counts retained
Classification annotates data without removing outliers from estimation
native_boundaries: Airbug rejects empty/nonfinite populations and supports singleton descriptive classification.
Unrepresentable finite-range fences serialize as null rather than invalid JSON numbers.
Multi-process estimate classification uses the declared process-median population; raw observation charts remain separate.
outlier_semantic_audit.validation: Two outlier tests passed: both tails and fence equality, zero-IQR core, extreme numeric range and JSON validity. Full 521-test MSRV gate includes contracts::outlier_reporting_preserves_extreme_observations_in_estimates.

contracts: Positive bootstrap resample count; confidence and significance strictly between zero and one.
Confidence changes percentile boundaries, not point estimates, bootstrap draws or their standard error.
Practical threshold changes practical decisions independently of significance.
native_differences: Airbug rejects infinite noise thresholds; pinned Criterion accepts positive infinity. Airbug uses percent units and a default 5% margin, Criterion uses a fractional threshold and defaults to 1%.
Airbug returns validation errors instead of setter panics. One bootstrap draw is supported with unavailable standard error.
Absolute bootstrap confidence is independent from history significance; comparison inference uses process populations and family adjustment as documented above.
